result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A's plan follows the rubric's order: define tokens by snapping to the nearest value, merge the duplicates, then rebuild components. It explains why that order works and hedges sensibly, for example noting that button height depends on line-height and suggesting screenshots before changes. B gives more concrete snap mappings but asserts things it can't see: it calls .btn-big's missing color a bug when .btn-big is likely used alongside .btn, and it states contrast ratios assuming a white background. Its plan also starts with 'bugs' rather than shared values. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B follows the right order: it defines tokens first, merges the near-duplicates next and rebuilds components after that, and it explains why that order works. It also avoids unsupported claims and hedges where it lacks information, such as button height depending on line-height. A quotes specific values well and gives concrete snap targets, but it overreaches. It calls the very different modal shadow 'near-identical' and assumes .btn-big renders dark text, though it is likely used with .btn. It also states AA contrast failures without knowing the background.
